open_questions: Low-significance secondary at phase 0.77 needs RV and follow-up photometry to confirm absence of stellar companion and rule out brown-dwarf occultation.
Centroid could not localize due to low SNR – high-resolution imaging or seeing-limited ground transit would directly confirm on-target.
One sector (62) shows a very poor depth measurement – monitoring to improve SoH would fully establish depth constancy.
dossier.public_summary: A small 450 ppm dip every 9.7 days repeats 12 times with a flat bottom that matches the size of the host star, implying a ~2 Earth-radius object. No bright nearby star can mimic it and there is no clear odd/even or strong binary secondary, so a planet is the best explanation. A weak secondary-like bump and an inconclusive centroid leave a bit of uncertainty that follow-up can resolve.

reasons.why: Planet-sized 1.94 R_E with flat-bottomed, full-duration transit favours planet; V shape absent and duration matches stellar density for K dwarf.
Secondary is only ~5 sigma vs best_brightening_snr 3.192, only 1.7x bump and offset from 0.5, not a phase 0.5 EB secondary; odd/even difference not significant, so no evidence for EB at twice period.
